subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real valued function f(x) = √([x] − x), where [x] is the greatest integer not exceeding x.

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the conditions the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use [x] ≤ x
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. State [x] ≤ x before drawing any conclusion.
steps.memory_tip: [x] is never above x, so [x] − x is never positive. The root then forces it to be exactly zero.
lines: By definition [x] ≤ x for every real x,
Both together force [x] − x = 0, that is [x] = x

recall.must_convey: That the root needs [x] − x ≥ 0 while the definition gives [x] − x ≤ 0, so the only survivors are the points where [x] = x.
accept: the greatest integer is at most x so the difference is at most zero
the root needs it non negative and the definition needs it non positive so it must be zero
bracket x equals x is the only possibility
greatest integer x kanna ekkuva raadu so difference zero avvali
the two conditions squeeze the expression to exactly zero

steps.why: The condition from the root points one way and the definition of the greatest integer function points the other, so only the points where the two meet at zero can survive.
common_mistakes: Reading [x] as the modulus of x and solving |x| − x ≥ 0 instead.
Writing [x] ≥ x, which reverses the definition.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.
steps.memory_tip: [2.7] = 2 and [−1.3] = −2, so [x] = x only on whole numbers, negative ones included.
lines: [x] = x holds only when x is an integer.
For any other x the inside of the root is negative.

lines.text: ∴ Domain = Z, the set of all integers

recall.must_convey: That the domain is the set of all integers, not an interval.
accept: Z including the negative integers and zero
only whole numbers are in the domain
the domain is a set of separate points not an interval

steps.why: For any x with a fractional part, [x] is strictly below x and the inside of the root is negative, so only the whole numbers remain.
common_mistakes: Answering R, or an interval, when the domain is a set of separated points.
Answering N, which loses the negative integers and 0.
